transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in because... I've had this really drastic shift in how I'm functioning at work. I manage production at a plant, and recently I went from just... launching non-stop redesign projects, calling our suppliers way after hours, and basically rewriting the entire shift plan by myself... to suddenly hitting a wall. Now I find myself completely unable to keep up with the very plans I just set in motion. It's gotten really bad, and I just need to figure out what's going on with me.

When you were launching all those redesign projects and calling suppliers late at night, how was your mood during that time? Did you feel unusually energetic, excited, or like you needed very little sleep?

Well, at the beginning of all that, I felt almost... electrically upbeat. Just really, really driven. But then it kind of turned into me being weirdly irritable. Like, if anyone at the plant questioned my ideas, I got so frustrated. It just felt like they were slowing down something that was completely obvious and important.

During that time when you were feeling electrically upbeat and irritable—launching all those projects and calling suppliers late—did you notice that you needed less sleep than usual? Like, were you sleeping fewer hours but still feeling rested and energized?

Yeah, exactly. I was sleeping... maybe two or three hours a night at most. But I wasn't tired at all. I would still show up at the plant the next morning feeling completely sharp and charged. It honestly just felt like sleep was optional, you know? Like it was just kind of inefficient and getting in the way of everything I needed to get done.

How long did that period last—when you were feeling electrically upbeat, sleeping only a few hours, launching all those projects, and feeling irritable? From start to finish, was it days, weeks, or longer?

I'm not exactly sure, honestly. It's a little hard to pin down the exact timeframe because time just felt... different when I was moving that fast. It definitely wasn't just a day or two, but I don't know if it was a full week or longer before I finally crashed. I just wasn't really keeping track of the days.
When you look back at that period of feeling electrically upbeat and irritable, launching all those projects—do you think it lasted at least a full week, or was it shorter than that?

I... I really don't know for sure. Like I said, I wasn't keeping track. I just know it was a few days at least, but I couldn't tell you if it made it to a full seven days. It's just a blur of working and not sleeping.

Looking back, do you think that period when you were feeling electrically upbeat, sleeping just a few hours, and working intensely—would you say it lasted at least 4 days in a row, or was it less than that?
Yeah, it was definitely at least four days in a row. I know that much. I remember starting the week like that and it kept going through most of the work week, so... yeah, four days for sure.

During that period when you were feeling electrically upbeat and working intensely—did you experience any beliefs that felt absolutely true to you at the time, but that others around you didn't share or thought were unrealistic? For example, did you feel like you had special abilities, or that you could accomplish things that most people couldn't?

Yeah, I did. I, um... I honestly believed I could fix the entire production workflow at work all by myself, and that I could do it faster than the whole consulting team we had brought in. People tried to point out concerns or tell me to slow down, but I just brushed them off. I was so sure of myself that failure didn't even seem possible to me at the time.

When you believed you could fix the entire production workflow faster than the consulting team, did you experience anything unusual like hearing voices, seeing things, or having thoughts that felt completely real but that you now realize didn't make sense?

No, nothing like that. I didn't hear voices or see things that weren't there. It was just... I just had this really intense, absolute confidence that I was right and everyone else was just moving too slow. But I wasn't hallucinating or anything.

You mentioned the intense, upbeat, irritable period lasted through most of the work week—that would be roughly 4 or 5 days. But I want to be clear: did that period of feeling electrically upbeat, sleeping only a few hours, and working intensely ever stretch into a full 7 days or longer before you crashed?
No, it wasn't a full week. It was just those four or maybe five days, and then I just completely ran out of gas. It definitely didn't last seven days.

The patient's current presentation is characterized by inability to function, inability to keep up with previously initiated projects, and a depressive crash following the elevated period. Without confirmed hypomanic episodes meeting full duration criteria, and with a current depressive presentation, major depressive disorder is the most appropriate diagnosis.
